newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX power settles lower amid mixed cash trading.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX power settles lower amid mixed cash trading.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled lower Tuesday as spot cash prices in the West traded mixed today amid unplanned plant outages in the Northwest and forecasts of unseasonably cool temperatures in the Southwest.
"It's the cooler weather more than anything else," a West Coast trader replied when asked for the main reason behind today's decline.
September Palo Verde (PV) settled down 91 cents to $29.77 a megawatt hour (MWh) just two cents above its session low.
October PV finished down 60 cents at $23.10. Deferred PV contracts ended flat to down 80 cents.
September California Oregon Border (COB) settled down 51 cents at $22.44 after traded between $22.50 and $23.20.
October COB finished down five cents at $21.70. Other COB months ended flat to down 10 cents.

In a mirror reversal of yesterday's activity, day-ahead prices in Southwest fell on forecasts of cooler-than-normal summer temperatures, while those in the Northwest rose on unplanned plant outages and reportedly buying from Bonneville Power Administration (BPA).
Day-ahead peak power at PV softened to $35.00-36.50 after traded as high as $40.00 Monday, and deliveries at COB firmed 50 cents to a dollar to $17.50-19.00 a MWh.
BPA, which has mostly been a seller of power over the last couple of months, said it is buying back some electricity to cover its needs as hydropower reservoirs are being re-filled.
Federal hydropower dams in the Northwest are subject to strict flow requirements during spring and summer months, when fish migration takes place.
Day-ahead power prices in the Northwest were also boosted by an unplanned outage at a 550 megawatt (MW) Jim Bridger unit in Wyoming and a 254 MW unit at Valmy in Nevada.
A 260 MW unit at the Hayden coal-fired power plant in Colorado was also said to be off line until Wednesday due to a tube leak, but this could not be immediately confirmed.
A 600 MW hydroturbine at the Grand Coulee dam in Washington may resume operation as early as tomorrow as opposed to the previous date of August 11, traders said.
The unit was shut in February for maintenance.
The 1,221 MW Palo Verde 2 nuclear power unit in Arizona began slowly coasting down to its September refueling outage.
The 750 MW Four Corners coal-fired unit 5 in New Mexico, shut earlier this month to repair a high pressure generator field, was planned to restart next week.
Damage to a fish ladder at the Bonneville Dam on the Columbia River in Oregon could reduce power output at the project by 200 MW for a month or two.
Final approval from the Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) to increase the intertie's capacity to 6,900 MW from 6,300 is expected later this week.

The latest six to 10 day forecasts showed the West would experience seasonal to slightly cooler-than-seasonal readings regionwide with a monsoonal flow bringing above-normal precipitation in the mountainous areas.
((--R Leong, New York Power Desk +1 212 859 1622))
